value.body: A clinical statistical programmer turns raw clinical trial data into analysis datasets, tables and figures that biostatisticians and regulators review. Employers include pharma companies, clinical research organisations and their analytics centres. A typical day involves writing and checking code, comparing outputs line by line, and documenting work for audits.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Stat, B.Math, statistics or life-science graduates

items.label: Common tools
items.value: SAS, R, data standards such as CDISC SDTM / ADaM

items.label: GATE Statistics (ST) paper
items.source: GATE 2025 Statistical and Performance Report, IIT Roorkee

items.label: Postgraduate students in statistics
items.source: AISHE (Ministry of Education) 2023-24, Table 13 (based on actual responses)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a pharma or clinical research company as trainee programmers after a coding and statistics test. A base programming certification in SAS or R is commonly asked for. Strong statistics from B.Stat or B.Math helps move toward biostatistician roles.

value.title: At a glance
items: Work is highly regulated, with strict checking and audit trails.
Next roles: senior programmer, lead programmer, biostatistician (often after a master's).
